description: destsize - strlen(dest) is computed as size_t without a check: if dest is longer than destsize (or unterminated within it), the size wraps to a huge value and I_strcpy copies past the buffer. Should clamp, or return when strlen(dest) >= destsize.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp I_strcat; test_q_shared.py keeps destsize >= strlen(dest) for this reason. Callers not yet audited for whether any can reach it.

description: Each '*' recurses at every remaining position with no memoisation, so patterns with several '*' that fail late take exponential time (and unbounded stack). Replace with the linear backtracking glob match.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp I_stricmpwild. Callers (and whether patterns can come from the network or console) not yet identified.

description: With one null argument the result is (int)(s1 - s0): a pointer difference truncated to 32 bits, so its sign depends on the other pointer's address. Same in I_strncmp (1423B47D0) and I_stricmp (1423B48E0, inlined). Should return a fixed -1/1.
evidence: src/universal/q_shared.cpp; null-pointer inputs in test_q_shared.py match the original only because both runs use the same heap address.

description: The Store build runs Havok's Visual Debugger server: while a level's navigation volumes load (141EBE450 -> 141EBC350) it creates the visual debugger and calls serve(25001), which creates an hkBsdSocket, binds it to INADDR_ANY (every interface) on TCP port 25001 and listens; the debugger then polls for and accepts clients every frame. A listening socket in a game client, speaking Havok's VDB protocol, which was never meant to face untrusted peers.
evidence: 141EBC350 (calls 142AE2510 then 142AE2740 with 0x61A9); 142A43730 binds sin_addr 0 and listens with backlog 2; serve verified in tests/differential/test_hkVisualDebugger.py. Reached in normal play by the level-load path (not yet observed in a running game).

description: When a zone's key is missing from the built-in table, fastfile loading asks a development key server over UDP at hard-coded internal addresses 10.150.4.43 / 10.150.97.133:10019. Dead in retail networks but still opens a socket and retries; should be removed.
evidence: pseudocode 14149E620/14149E6D0/14149E870; caller 14149EAC0, gated by 141FBC390(0). Private addresses: cannot reach the internet.

description: Com_Error_ feeds a crash reporter that sends a Google Analytics event (ssl.google-analytics.com/collect, tid UA-69466650-2) with a persistent machine GUID from HKLM\\SOFTWARE\\Activision\\HardwareSurvey, writes crash_reports/*.gltn with that GUID and the Windows volume object id, and launches CrashUploader.exe through system(). Sends data off the machine without the user's knowledge; the blocking curl_easy_perform can stall error handling; system() runs whatever CrashUploader.exe is found on the search path.
evidence: pseudocode 1423B87C0 (strings), 1423B9AB0 (curl_global_init); pseudocode 1423B8BA0 (gltn writer, system call), 1423B9DE0 (report); call chain Com_Error_ 142210B90 -> 1423B9F70; report via 1423F1F80 -> 1423B9DE0. docs/network.md section 3.

description: A datagram received on an IPv6 socket leaves the sender's address where WSARecvFrom put it (sockaddr_in6 layout: family, port and flow info in the first 8 bytes) instead of moving sin6_addr to the start as the reset path does, and m_family is never set from the received address: the caller gets a wrong IPv6 peer address. IPv4 is handled correctly.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp receiveFrom (success, AF_INET6) against its reset path; tests/differential/test_bdPlatformSocket.py covers both. Reachable whenever Demonware uses an IPv6 socket.

description: Copies ai_addrlen bytes of each result into a 16-byte stack sockaddr_in without checking the length: a longer address would overflow the stack. The hints ask for AF_INET only, so Winsock returns 16-byte addresses today. The bdSockAddrs it fills also never get m_family set.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp getHostByName; the faithful test uses ai_addrlen <= 16. No current input reaches the overflow.

description: For AF_INET6, a failed WSASocketA is logged and then setsockopt(IPV6_V6ONLY) is still called on the invalid handle, which fails and logs a second, misleading error before returning -1. For AF_INET a failed socket() is not logged at all.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformSocket-xboxone.cpp create; covered by test_bdPlatformSocket.py (sockets that come back INVALID_SOCKET).

description: On WSAENOTCONN it calls checkSocketException, drops the result and falls through into the WSAEMSGSIZE case, so a receive on an unconnected socket reports BD_NET_MSG_SIZE. send handles the same error properly (BD_NET_CONNECTION_RESET or BD_NET_NOT_CONNECTED). A missing return in the original switch.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformStreamSocket-xboxone.cpp receive; covered by test_bdPlatformStreamSocket.py (error 10057). Reachable when the lobby connection drops before it is established.

description: Always builds an AF_INET sockaddr from the address's first four bytes, whatever m_family says, so a TCP connection to an IPv6 address (on a socket create made with AF_INET6) can never succeed.
evidence: src/libs/DemonWareGDK/bdPlatform/bdPlatformSocket/bdPlatformStreamSocket-xboxone.cpp connect; covered by test_bdPlatformStreamSocket.py (all families). Reachable only if Demonware is given an IPv6 server address.

description: r_refreshRate is registered with the domain [1, 240] (default 60, latched). Dvar_SetVariant (1423A21C0) refuses a value outside a dvar's domain and keeps the old one, so nothing above 240 Hz can be set: the first-run hardware detection (141DA9620) sets the fastest mode's rate and is refused on a >240 Hz monitor (r_refreshRate stays 60), choosing 360 in the menu or console is refused, and the fullscreen swap chain (141DA7A00) picks the mode closest to the value that stuck. Mode enumeration has no limit and com_maxfps goes to 1000, so the domain is the whole cap.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_refresh_rate.py test_refresh_rate_domain (the original registers 60, 1, 240); Dvar_SetVariant 1423A21C0 pseudocode (Dvar_ValueInDomain false -> message, value kept). Every player on a >240 Hz monitor hits it.

description: Looks at only the first 128 entries of the monitor's mode list (min(dx_modeCount, 128)). The list is sorted smallest size first and DXGI_ENUM_MODES_SCALING makes it long, so on monitors with more than 128 modes the largest resolutions (usually the native one) get no refresh rates in the settings menu.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_refresh_rate.py test_native_mode_past_128 (original lists nothing for 2560x1440 at indexes 135..139); 1420E7490 cmovle with 0x80. Reachable whenever a monitor reports more than 128 modes.

description: The display-mode comparator never returns 0: for equal sizes it returns -1 if a's rate is lower, else 1, so two modes with the same rate each compare greater than the other. qsort's contract is broken (the order of equal-rate duplicates is unspecified); 141DAA790 merges such duplicates right after, so nothing visible follows from it today.
evidence: tests/differential/test_r_init.py (equal-rate pairs return 1 both ways in the original); 141DAA73E..141DAA789.

description: With r_vsync on, an AMD adapter (dx_vendor 2) and dx_remoteScreenUpdateNesting nonzero (a loading screen is being drawn from its own thread), the present path first sleeps trunc(1000 / r_refreshRate) - 2 ms: a pacer built on the requested rate rather than the mode in use, at Sleep granularity. In normal play the nesting count is 0 and it never runs (earlier reading, before decompiling: every AMD present).
evidence: 141D4681D..141D46861 (dx_remoteScreenUpdateNesting at 1486F0D90, r_vsync, dx_vendor 1486F0E30 == 2; Sleep); tests/differential/test_r_present.py. Loading screens only.

description: Mouse sensitivity follows the field of view in hip fire as well as ADS: the movement is multiplied by tan(current vertical half-FOV) / 0.47780272, the tangent of the default cg_fov 65 at 4:3. Raising cg_fov raises hip-fire sensitivity (x1.317 at cg_fov 80, x1.570 at 90, x2.242 at 110, before any lens adjustment), and the factor isn't 1 at the default either when the cgame's lens model narrows the view. Aim feel changes with the FOV setting and with every zoom.
evidence: tests/differential/test_cl_input.py (the scale is linear in the cgame tangent at +0x131D6C); 1413AE69B..1413AE6E7. Every mouse player hits it.

description: m_filter only halves the frame's movement: the averaging with the other buffer that the name and the double buffer suggest (Quake 3's m_filter) is gone, so the option acts as a hidden 0.5x sensitivity.
evidence: tests/differential/test_cl_input.py; 1413ACC5D..1413ACC6D (mulss by 0.5, no add of the other buffer).

description: m_mouseAcceleration adds acceleration * speed, with speed in counts per whole millisecond of client frame time (cls_frametime is an int): at frame rates above a few hundred fps the integer frame time jumps between values (2/3/4 ms) or reads 1 for any shorter frame, so the same hand speed gives a jittering sensitivity; frame time 0 would divide by zero (CL_MouseMove returns before that).
evidence: 1413ACE68..1413ACE9F; tests/differential/test_cl_input.py covers frame times 1..33. Reachable with m_mouseAcceleration > 0 (menu: MouseAcceleration).

description: With no cgame (encrypted cg array pointer 0) or a localClientNum past the array, the FOV tangent is read from a null cg_t, address 0x131D6C, instead of falling back to 1.
evidence: tests/differential/test_cl_input.py (cases with pointer 0 and localClientNum >= count). Not reachable from CL_MouseMove in play as far as known: it returns early without an active local client.

description: The view angles are accumulated in single precision (cl +0xB8CC yaw, +0xB8C8 pitch, never wrapped here): each frame's turn is rounded to the float grid of the current angle. At MW2019-style rates (about 0.01 degrees a count) and high frame rates a frame's turn is a few counts, and once the yaw has wound up to thousands of degrees the grid (0.004 degrees at 36000) is comparable to a count, so slow movements are rounded away or doubled and the same movement split over more frames ends at a different angle.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_sensitivity.py test_mouse_move_accumulates_in_double (36000 - 0.4 ulp plus one 0.1-sensitivity count); 1413AE974..1413AE984, 1413AEA4E..1413AEA5A.

description: Without depth of field (cg+0x131D28 & 0x30000 == 0, i.e. normal play) the lens is focused at 500 mm (focus = max(500, f+1)), and a lens focused that close sees less: tan(vertical/2) = 7/f - 7/500 instead of 7/f. The player's FOV setting (horizontal at 16:9) therefore shows narrower than set: 65 -> 62.95, 80 -> 78.31, 90 -> 88.56, 100 -> 98.81, 110 -> 109.05, 120 -> 119.28 degrees at 16:9. Aimed-down-sights zooms (weapon lenses) are narrowed the same way, but those are the shipped zooms.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_fov.py test_hip_fov_is_exact (runs the original CG_CalcFOVfromLens: the original shows at least 0.5 degrees less at every setting); 1405B2D19-1405B2D77. Every player in normal play.

description: cg_fov_default (the FOV setting, horizontal at 16:9) is registered 65-120; MW2019, which uses the same unit, allows 60-120.
evidence: tests/enhanced/test_fov.py test_fov_minimum_60 (the original registers 80, 65, 120); 1423ABEE9.

description: Copies cg_fov_default (or cg_fov_default_thirdperson) into cg_fov unchanged, but cg_fov's readers take it as a horizontal FOV at 4:3: 1400C44A0 computes tan(cg_fov/2)*0.75 against the view's tanHalfFovY (a ratio that is 1.37, not 1, at the default 80), and CG_CalcFOVfromLens/1405B2E80 build their lens from cg_fov*0.75 when cg_drawMinimap is set. The setting means the 16:9 horizontal FOV everywhere else (1405B2E80 uses 9/16; config.ini: 'Horizontal field of view in degrees assuming 16:9 aspect ratio').
evidence: 1408E3D40, 1400C44A0, 1405B2E80 pseudocode. Normal play does not use the cg_drawMinimap branch; what 1400D1950 (1400C44A0's caller) does with the ratio is not known yet.

description: Mouse movement made while the game is not in front is counted and lands on the view when it comes back: the mouse is registered with RIDEV_INPUTSINK so the raw input thread keeps counting in the background, IN_MouseMove returns without taking the counts while another window is in front (and IN_Frame skips it while the window is inactive), and the first frame back takes it all.
evidence: tests/differential/test_win_input.py (background cases leave win_rawMouseDx/Dy untouched); tests/enhanced/test_raw_input.py test_background_movement_is_not_counted. Every alt-tab with the mouse moving triggers it.

description: The raw input thread polls: GetRawInputBuffer, then Sleep(1) (about 1 ms with timeBeginPeriod(1) at 1423BF710), so a mouse report waits up to about a millisecond before IN_MouseMove can take it.
evidence: 1423F4C9B Sleep(1) in the loop; tests/differential/test_win_input.py. Every frame.

description: Every RAWMOUSE report's lLastX/lLastY is added whatever usFlags says: an absolute device (MOUSE_MOVE_ABSOLUTE: tablets, remote desktop, some virtual machines) adds screen positions (0..65535) as movement and spins the view. The counters are 32-bit and wrap.
evidence: 1423F4C03..1423F4C62 test only dwType; tests/differential/test_win_input.py feeds flags 1 to both copies. Reachable with any absolute pointing device.

description: The window thread polls its message queue with Sleep(1) between passes: key and button presses wait up to about a millisecond before the window procedure queues them, and every message the render thread SendMessageA's to the window (0x8043 Present, 0x8042 swap chain, 0x8044 fullscreen) blocks until the window thread wakes, adding up to a millisecond to every Present and making frame times uneven.
evidence: 1423F4AAE Sleep(1); SendMessageA(win_hWnd, 0x8043) in 141D46720; tests/differential/test_win_input.py. Every frame.

description: The swap chain uses the blit model (sub_141DA7A00 fills DXGI_SWAP_EFFECT_DISCARD, flags ALLOW_MODE_SWITCH): in a window or borderless the desktop compositor copies every frame (a frame or more of extra latency, no independent flip), and with r_vsync 0 a window cannot tear, so it stays capped at the desktop refresh with compositor queueing.
evidence: 141DA7A60 Windowed 1 / SwapEffect 0 (qword at +38h), 141DA7A68 Flags 2; 141DAB322 SendMessageA 0x8042; tests/differential/test_r_swapchain.py. Every frame.

description: Present is not called by the thread that finished the frame: it SendMessageA(win_hWnd, 0x8043, r_vsync)s the window thread, whose window procedure presents. Each present waits for the window thread to pick the message up (up to its 1 ms sleep, B0043) plus two thread switches, and while a vsync Present blocks, the window thread cannot pump keyboard and mouse messages.
evidence: 141D46879 SendMessageA(win_hWnd, 0x8043, vsync, 0); the window procedure presents (swap chain vtable +40h); tests/differential/test_r_present.py. Every frame.

description: Nothing makes the CPU wait for the display before sampling input: with vsync on (or a GPU-bound frame) the main thread reads the mouse and builds the usercmd as soon as it can, and the frame then queues behind earlier ones (r_maxFrameLatency only limits the device queue, and the blit model adds the compositor's). Input is up to the queue depth in frames old when it reaches the screen.
evidence: IN_Frame (1423BDB70) runs from 1413BFDE0 before CL_CreateCmd with no wait; no waitable object is made in 141DAB250; tests/differential/test_in_frame.py. Every frame.

description: With SLI, the NV_GET_CURRENT_SLI_STATE currentAFRIndex is copied into the remembered index even when NvAPI_D3D_GetCurrentSLIState failed, so the uninitialised stack value is compared on the next frame.
evidence: 141D467E5 reads currentAFRIndex, 141D467EE tests the status only for the flag, 141D46801 stores it regardless; tests/differential/test_r_present.py. SLI only.

description: When the IDXGIDevice1 -> IDXGIAdapter1 -> IDXGIFactory1 chain or the swap chain creation fails, the function returns without releasing the interfaces it already holds: a COM reference leak per failed attempt (the caller then retries windowed).
evidence: 141DAB2B3/2D2/2F1/32D: JS to the epilogue (141DAB573/57B) past the Releases at 141DAB36D..383; tests/differential/test_r_swapchain.py. Failure path only.

description: The camera the GPU draws is fixed when CG_DrawActiveFrame builds the refdef, a whole main-thread frame before the render thread draws it: the render thread works a frame behind (R_EndFrame hands the frontend data over and the main thread builds the next frame meanwhile), and mouse movement that arrives in between waits for the next frame. Rust-test's renderer rereads the mouse right before recording the camera (peek_motion).
evidence: docs/late-latch.md (the path, where the time goes); 141DCAD40 publishes the frontend data to RB_RenderThread (141D47510) and R_BeginFrame flips to the other buffer
